ByteBrain is ByteDance’s AI for Infrastructure (AI4Infra) platform, dedicated to improving the efficiency, reliability, and intelligence of large-scale infrastructure systems through AI and machine learning. ByteBrain supports a wide range of infrastructure domains, including AI data center supply chains, AIOps, Operations Research and AgentOps, powering infrastructure optimization at massive scale.

Why This Role Is Unique

This role sits at the intersection of: Operations Research × AIOps × AI for Infra

You will have the opportunity to solve some of the most challenging optimization problems behind large-scale AI datacenters while pioneering the next generation of AI-powered decision-making systems, where LLMs, and optimization algorithms work together to improve efficiency, resource utilization, and operational intelligence across ByteDance's global infrastructure.

Responsibilities

Design and develop AI, machine learning, and optimization algorithms to improve the efficiency, reliability, and performance of large-scale infrastructure systems and AI supply chain. Areas may include AIOps, operations research, software engineering, AgentOps, and system optimization.
Drive the deployment, scaling, and continuous improvement of algorithms in production environments, supporting large-scale services.
Identify optimization opportunities and emerging challenges from real-world infrastructure scenarios, translating them into impactful research and engineering solutions.
Conduct cutting-edge research and publish high-quality papers in top-tier conferences and journals.

With the large-scale adoption of LLMs and AI agents, traditional cloud-native infrastructure can no longer meet the ultra-high performance and elasticity requirements of AI workloads. This topic conducts systematic research across the entire AI infrastructure stack:

Network and Observability: Research intelligent fault localization and root cause analysis for large-scale AI clusters, combined with intelligent tuning of time-series databases to improve cluster stability.

Industry experience applying AI and optimization techniques to real-world infrastructure challenges, such as:

Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by end of year 2027. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Team Introduction:

The Applied Machine Learning Ark team combines system engineering and machine learning to develop and operate Large Language Model (LLM) service platforms that offer businesses Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) solutions, serving both large model providers and downstream users. The US team drives the design, development, and operation of MaaS solutions across the US and international markets outside mainland China. We are building full-stack, end-to-end solutions spanning text and multimodal LLM algorithms, LLM training/fine-tuning/inference frameworks, prompt engineering, model alignment, and intelligent agent systems. Beyond model serving, we operate large-scale log analytics pipelines that process massive volumes of invocation logs from text models, multimodal models, and agent systems — extracting usage patterns, quality signals, and actionable insights to inform model improvement, system optimization, and product decisions through continuous, data-driven feedback loops. We are actively seeking talented engineers and researchers specializing in Large Language Models and AI Agent systems to join our dynamic team.

With foundation models gradually being applied in real ToB scenarios, AI system optimization now extends beyond the foundation model itself to include a complex business system composed of the model, prompt, memory, tools, skills, workflow, and the external environment. Compared to offline benchmarks, real-world cases offer greater potential for optimization but also present challenges such as larger data volumes, higher noise levels, more diverse scenarios, greater structural heterogeneity, and limited user feedback, making them difficult to be directly utilized.

Relying on the real-world data accumulated on the Volcano Ark case platform, this project aims to unify logs, cases, feedback, and environmental information into structured objects that are understandable, and attributable, and optimizable. By integrating AI-assisted tools to guide users in providing efficient feedback, it aims to build an AI data flywheel system tailored to real scenarios. This system will both support foundation model iteration and address issues related to environment, memory, tools, and workflows within the business system, focusing on developing agent optimization capabilities that enhance SA/FDE’s efficiency in supporting customers.

jobs.description:
We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to take our healthcare customers from scoping calls to production.

Healthcare administration is a $1T opportunity that is largely inaccessible to AI today.

Asteroid gives customers programmable APIs to the healthcare systems where work gets done, and lets them rapidly convert manual workflows into AI-assisted automations.

We are a YC W25 company. Our agents run a quarter of a million operations a month across 300+ healthcare portals and systems. We have seven figures of revenue and are growing 30%+ month over month. Customer churn is exceptionally low, and we pride ourselves on strong relationships with our customers.

Why This Role Exists

Large parts of the fragmented healthcare industry rely on legacy systems that have no APIs. AI is capable of work like prior authorization, referral intake and patient scheduling, yet today whole teams still do these tasks by hand.

Asteroid's platform opens up access to these systems and makes it possible to automate any workflow on them. The FDE role exists to turn manual healthcare work into browser, computer-use or API-based automations on our platform.

You will work directly with healthcare customers from day one and make sure they succeed on Asteroid. What you learn from them feeds back to our engineering team and improves how we automate healthcare work.

What You'll Own

Scoping.
You join sales and onboarding calls with healthcare teams. You learn how they do the work today and define with them what the workflow looks like and what "done" means: inputs, outputs, edge cases, system access and success criteria.

Building.
You turn that scope into a production workflow on the Asteroid platform using our AI assistant or our MCP server. You test the workflow against real portals.

Running.
Once a workflow is live, you triage early failures, fix issues and tune reliability and cost.

Account ownership.
You are the first responder in each customer's Slack channel. You answer, reproduce, fix what you can and escalate what needs engineering. You run check-ins with our enterprise accounts and spot where they can do more with us. This may include traveling to see customers on site.

Example Workflows You Might Work On

Prior authorization submission and status tracking in payer portals (Availity, UHC, Aetna and others)
Eligibility and benefits checks before a visit
EHR write-back: patient demographics, notes, documents, orders
Patient creation and scheduling in practice management systems
Referral intake from fax and provider portals
Enrollment in marketplace and carrier portals
Legacy and Citrix-hosted EHRs through computer-use agents

What You'll Contribute To

Product direction. As we scale to eight-figure ARR, your insights will shape where the company goes.
Dozens of healthcare accounts running real work on Asteroid.
The day-to-day product experience. You will work with a high-performing engineering team to improve the platform in ways small and large.
The shape and design of our APIs, which the next wave of healthcare companies will build on.

CEO, AI Expert Network Platform
Remote, North America · Backed by Venture Studio · Product built, first pilots starting

The company
We're a venture studio, and we've built an AI platform that lets investment firms and corporates run their own expert network. Teams find, engage, and pay the right experts on their own terms.
The product is built and our first PE and VC pilots are about to start. We're all in on it, and we're looking for the CEO to take it from here.

The market
Expert calls used to be a hedge fund tool. Now they're a standard part of how PE funds, consultants, and corporate teams get smart on a market fast. The industry behind them is worth roughly $3 billion a year, and the number of firms buying has more than doubled since 2022.

The problem
For over twenty years, the big expert networks have run the same play, and it costs funds three ways:
Time.
Every search runs on someone else's clock, through a database they own.
Money.
Every hour on the phone carries a premium.
Quality.
The expert is the best match on their list, not the best person for the question.

And when the project wraps, the middleman keeps the relationship, which is the part that actually compounds.

Why now
The old model depended on a huge proprietary database and a big team working the phones. That advantage is fading fast. AI can now find the right expert almost anywhere, reach them directly, and handle the admin that used to take a team.

Our bet
Our bet is that firms should own their expert network, not rent it. Cutting out the middleman improves all three at once: firms move faster, spend less, and get better experts. And the relationships that compound finally stay with the firm.
We funded the build, put world-class builders on it, and we're the first cheque in.

How it works
From the client's seat, the platform turns a rough question into a paid, documented expert engagement, with no middleman in the way.

It starts with a conversation. Our AI helps you shape the brief: the goal, the expertise you need, budget, timeline, and how you want the insight delivered. The brief gets its own page and a link you can share.

Then our AI goes hunting. Our proprietary people search pulls up a pool of relevant experts you can contact right away. Keep the ones you like and run it again with a sharper ask.

Outreach is your call. Our AI can handle it, or we'll hand you a script and a link to your brief so the ask comes from you. Personal asks get more yeses, so we make them easy.

Experts join in under 30 seconds, see the whole brief, and can ask questions before they say yes. Payment runs through the platform, so every engagement is documented and auditable. Compliance teams love that part.

The platform captures the insights from every engagement and keeps them in one place, so nothing you learn walks out the door.

Every project adds to a bench of experts you own, and it gets more valuable with every brief.

The role
From day one, it's yours to run: strategy, revenue, fundraising, and the team. Year one comes down to four jobs, in this order:
Turn pilots into paying clients.
Get our first pilot funds paying, then make them your best references. You'll set pricing, close the first contracts, and build a sales motion that works without a warm intro.
Raise the next round.
Take real traction to investors and lead the raise that funds what comes next. If you've sat on the other side of the table, you know what they'll want to see.
Build the team.
Make the first key hires and set the bar for everyone who follows. Who you hire first decides what the company becomes.
Expand beyond funds.
Corporate strategy and corp dev teams buy expert calls too. Once the fund motion works, that market is yours to open.

Who you are
You've either bought expert calls or sold them. Ideally both.

Maybe you spent years in PE or VC paying premium rates for calls that missed the mark. Maybe you worked at one of the big expert networks and saw exactly where the model cracks. Either way, you know this problem from the inside and already have opinions on how to fix it.

We don't expect one person to have everything. You have a real spike in at least one of these, and if you have both, even better:

Network and sales.
You can sell to funds, and you know how investment teams buy, who signs, and what gets a contract over the line. You have a network to sell into, and by now you're probably running through the first funds you'd call.
Product and building.
You've built something from scratch before, a company or a new business inside a bigger one, and you're itching to do it again. You're fluent in AI products and can shape what gets built next, even if you don't write code.

Whichever side you lead with, you'll be the one closing the first contracts. You can lead a raise, and investors take you seriously from the first meeting. You're based in North America and comfortable running a remote company.

What you get
A running start and a real stake in what you build.
A working product ready for its first clients, so you can start selling on day one.
Us in your corner. We've already put real money in, and we have every reason to help you win.
Meaningful equity and competitive cash. We haven't locked the final structure, and we'd rather shape it with the right person than hand over a template.
The freedom to work from anywhere in North America.
A real shot at changing how a big, entrenched industry works.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Healthcare)
new_jobs.description:
We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to take our healthcare customers from scoping calls to production.

Healthcare administration is a $1T opportunity that is largely inaccessible to AI today.

Asteroid gives customers programmable APIs to the healthcare systems where work gets done, and lets them rapidly convert manual workflows into AI-assisted automations.

We are a YC W25 company. Our agents run a quarter of a million operations a month across 300+ healthcare portals and systems. We have seven figures of revenue and are growing 30%+ month over month. Customer churn is exceptionally low, and we pride ourselves on strong relationships with our customers.

Why This Role Exists

Large parts of the fragmented healthcare industry rely on legacy systems that have no APIs. AI is capable of work like prior authorization, referral intake and patient scheduling, yet today whole teams still do these tasks by hand.

Asteroid's platform opens up access to these systems and makes it possible to automate any workflow on them. The FDE role exists to turn manual healthcare work into browser, computer-use or API-based automations on our platform.

You will work directly with healthcare customers from day one and make sure they succeed on Asteroid. What you learn from them feeds back to our engineering team and improves how we automate healthcare work.

What You'll Own

Scoping.
You join sales and onboarding calls with healthcare teams. You learn how they do the work today and define with them what the workflow looks like and what "done" means: inputs, outputs, edge cases, system access and success criteria.

Building.
You turn that scope into a production workflow on the Asteroid platform using our AI assistant or our MCP server. You test the workflow against real portals.

Running.
Once a workflow is live, you triage early failures, fix issues and tune reliability and cost.

Account ownership.
You are the first responder in each customer's Slack channel. You answer, reproduce, fix what you can and escalate what needs engineering. You run check-ins with our enterprise accounts and spot where they can do more with us. This may include traveling to see customers on site.

Example Workflows You Might Work On

Prior authorization submission and status tracking in payer portals (Availity, UHC, Aetna and others)
Eligibility and benefits checks before a visit
EHR write-back: patient demographics, notes, documents, orders
Patient creation and scheduling in practice management systems
Referral intake from fax and provider portals
Enrollment in marketplace and carrier portals
Legacy and Citrix-hosted EHRs through computer-use agents

What You'll Contribute To

Product direction. As we scale to eight-figure ARR, your insights will shape where the company goes.
Dozens of healthcare accounts running real work on Asteroid.
The day-to-day product experience. You will work with a high-performing engineering team to improve the platform in ways small and large.
The shape and design of our APIs, which the next wave of healthcare companies will build on.
The playbook we use for every healthcare deployment.

Qualifications & Requirements

A track record of building. You have built something real, such as a product with users. You are comfortable with scripts, APIs, logs and debugging.
Experience solving problems with LLMs. You can identify where models fail and reason about the trade-offs in reliability, cost and speed between LLM calls, API calls and deterministic scripts. You do not need to be an ML engineer.
Healthcare knowledge. You have worked in healthcare operations, built software for healthcare or studied it. You know what a prior auth, an eligibility check and a write-back are.
Customer skills. You can hold a conversation with a healthcare team, ask questions and turn the answers into a clear written scope.
Location. You are in San Francisco or able to relocate within three months. This is an in-office role, five days a week. We cannot sponsor visas.

One or two years of work experience is ideal. Strong new graduates are welcome.

Strong plus

You understand how computer-use agents work
Direct experience with an EHR, clearinghouse or payer portal as an operator or integrator

Not Required

A computer science degree, a clinical license, a previous FDE title, years of experience or an ML research background

Who Should Apply

A health-tech engineer a year or two in, who kept getting pulled into implementations and realized that was the part you liked
An engineer who has built with LLMs at work or in a serious side project, knows healthcare from a job, an internship or study, and wants to deploy agents where the stakes are real
A new graduate in CS, biomedical engineering or health informatics with LLM projects and a healthcare internship
A junior solutions or implementation engineer at an EHR, clearinghouse or prior auth vendor who wants to build with frontier AI instead of around it

If you understand how models work, you have seen healthcare's manual work up close, and you can build, this role was written for you.

Why Asteroid

You work at the frontier.
We have run computer-use agents on high-stakes workflows for two years. As far as we know, we were the first to deploy computer-use models in healthcare. We work with the labs, get early model access and publish what we learn. For example, we were an early-access partner for Anthropic's computer-use tool (our write-up).

Your work changes how healthcare runs.
Prior auth decides whether a patient gets treatment this week. Referral intake decides whether they get seen at all. Enrollment decides whether they have coverage. Our agents run inside these processes every day, for oncology care navigators, hospice technology companies, prior-auth platforms and AI scribes. Every workflow you ship removes real hours of manual work, and the effect reaches patients.

An extremely talent-dense team.
Everyone here builds, and everyone here ships. You will learn fast, be trusted early and own accounts in your first month.

We are growing fast.
Our agents already do years of human work every month, running hundreds of thousands of operations across EHRs and payer portals. Demand is ahead of our capacity to deploy. That is why this role exists, and why the work you do shows up directly in revenue.

CEO, AI Expert Network Platform
Remote, North America · Backed by Venture Studio · Product built, first pilots starting

The company
We're a venture studio, and we've built an AI platform that lets investment firms and corporates run their own expert network. Teams find, engage, and pay the right experts on their own terms.
The product is built and our first PE and VC pilots are about to start. We're all in on it, and we're looking for the CEO to take it from here.

The market
Expert calls used to be a hedge fund tool. Now they're a standard part of how PE funds, consultants, and corporate teams get smart on a market fast. The industry behind them is worth roughly $3 billion a year, and the number of firms buying has more than doubled since 2022.

The problem
For over twenty years, the big expert networks have run the same play, and it costs funds three ways:
Time.
Every search runs on someone else's clock, through a database they own.
Money.
Every hour on the phone carries a premium.
Quality.
The expert is the best match on their list, not the best person for the question.

And when the project wraps, the middleman keeps the relationship, which is the part that actually compounds.

Why now
The old model depended on a huge proprietary database and a big team working the phones. That advantage is fading fast. AI can now find the right expert almost anywhere, reach them directly, and handle the admin that used to take a team.

Our bet
Our bet is that firms should own their expert network, not rent it. Cutting out the middleman improves all three at once: firms move faster, spend less, and get better experts. And the relationships that compound finally stay with the firm.
We funded the build, put world-class builders on it, and we're the first cheque in.

How it works
From the client's seat, the platform turns a rough question into a paid, documented expert engagement, with no middleman in the way.

It starts with a conversation. Our AI helps you shape the brief: the goal, the expertise you need, budget, timeline, and how you want the insight delivered. The brief gets its own page and a link you can share.

Then our AI goes hunting. Our proprietary people search pulls up a pool of relevant experts you can contact right away. Keep the ones you like and run it again with a sharper ask.

Outreach is your call. Our AI can handle it, or we'll hand you a script and a link to your brief so the ask comes from you. Personal asks get more yeses, so we make them easy.

Experts join in under 30 seconds, see the whole brief, and can ask questions before they say yes. Payment runs through the platform, so every engagement is documented and auditable. Compliance teams love that part.

The platform captures the insights from every engagement and keeps them in one place, so nothing you learn walks out the door.

Every project adds to a bench of experts you own, and it gets more valuable with every brief.

The role
From day one, it's yours to run: strategy, revenue, fundraising, and the team. Year one comes down to four jobs, in this order:
Turn pilots into paying clients.
Get our first pilot funds paying, then make them your best references. You'll set pricing, close the first contracts, and build a sales motion that works without a warm intro.
Raise the next round.
Take real traction to investors and lead the raise that funds what comes next. If you've sat on the other side of the table, you know what they'll want to see.
Build the team.
Make the first key hires and set the bar for everyone who follows. Who you hire first decides what the company becomes.
Expand beyond funds.
Corporate strategy and corp dev teams buy expert calls too. Once the fund motion works, that market is yours to open.

Who you are
You've either bought expert calls or sold them. Ideally both.

Maybe you spent years in PE or VC paying premium rates for calls that missed the mark. Maybe you worked at one of the big expert networks and saw exactly where the model cracks. Either way, you know this problem from the inside and already have opinions on how to fix it.

We don't expect one person to have everything. You have a real spike in at least one of these, and if you have both, even better:

Network and sales.
You can sell to funds, and you know how investment teams buy, who signs, and what gets a contract over the line. You have a network to sell into, and by now you're probably running through the first funds you'd call.
Product and building.
You've built something from scratch before, a company or a new business inside a bigger one, and you're itching to do it again. You're fluent in AI products and can shape what gets built next, even if you don't write code.

Whichever side you lead with, you'll be the one closing the first contracts. You can lead a raise, and investors take you seriously from the first meeting. You're based in North America and comfortable running a remote company.

What you get
A running start and a real stake in what you build.
A working product ready for its first clients, so you can start selling on day one.
Us in your corner. We've already put real money in, and we have every reason to help you win.
Meaningful equity and competitive cash. We haven't locked the final structure, and we'd rather shape it with the right person than hand over a template.
The freedom to work from anywhere in North America.
A real shot at changing how a big, entrenched industry works.
